key_insight: Stochastic Neumann inverse-Hessian estimates can amplify skewness, while antithetic pairing cancels odd-order noise terms when the reference Hessian is exact.
engineering_relevance: More reliable hypergradients can improve bilevel learning pipelines exposed to corrupted labels, outliers, heterogeneous data, or class imbalance.
method: Mirror each sampled Hessian around a reference Hessian and average the paired Neumann estimates.
Cancel odd-order perturbations with an exact reference; bound residual odd-order contributions linearly in reference error otherwise.
Modify the Hessian-vector step to build ANE-SGD and ANE-VR, with recursive variance reduction in ANE-VR.
evidence_signal: Across four task families with 20 seeds each, ANE-based methods report 4–25% lower loss than the best baseline, including 25% lower test loss and 54% higher test R-squared in robust regression.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on reference-Hessian accuracy; assess the cost of constructing the reference and computing paired estimates.
paper_title: Your Hypergradient is Skewed: Antithetic Neumann Estimation for Bilevel Optimization
